referred_to: the Indiana Attorney General and the local prosecuting attorney
summary: The SBOA began after a complaint on April 9, 2024 that about 20 town checks were missing. It reports that from July 1 to September 23, 2024 Clerk-Treasurer Shane Williams-Inez used town debit cards 65 times to send $10,500.30 through the money-transfer service Remitly, none with an invoice or a documented town purpose (31 of the transfers, $5,345.05, came from internet addresses in the Philippines), and that he paid $1,019.30 for fireworks for an event held by a nonprofit he had helped incorporate. It lists a further $38,300.70 of purchases the town council had not approved, many without invoices, including payments to four "deputy clerks" made to their businesses rather than through payroll. The report also says a $13,660 snow-plowing check went to the council president's employer with no contract provided; that Williams-Inez and the council president made three $2,000 payments to one deputy clerk's company without invoices, and the president signed one of those checks (October 1, 2024); and that council minutes show only one member questioning why financial reports were not being presented. Williams-Inez resigned effective September 28, 2024; the council accepted the resignation on September 30. In January 2026 the Attorney General's office said it had received the report and was reviewing it for next steps. As of November 8, 2026 the guide found no criminal charges and no civil case to recover the money, after checking local news, the Attorney General's news releases and Indiana's public court records (MyCase).
notes: Charges, as summarized on report page 34, are to Williams-Inez: $11,519.60 for purchases without a town purpose ($10,500.30 Remitly plus $1,019.30 fireworks) and $10,621.50 in special investigation costs. Exit conference December 16, 2025 with the former and current clerk-treasurers, the council president, a council member and the town marshal. The report does not include an official response.
